items.definition: To have enough money to buy or do something.
examples: We can't afford a holiday abroad this year.
Houses in the city centre are too expensive for most young people to afford.

items.definition: Something you buy for much less than its usual price.
examples: At only twenty pounds, the coat was a bargain.
I found a few real bargains at the charity shop.

items.definition: Money that a shop gives back to you when you return something you have bought.
examples: The camera stopped working, so I asked for a refund.
You can get a full refund if you return the item within 28 days.

items.definition: A person who buys goods and services for their own use.
examples: Consumers are becoming more aware of where their clothes are made.
The new law is designed to protect consumers from misleading adverts.

items.definition: Costing more than it is worth.
examples: The food at the airport is overpriced and not very good.
I thought the trainers were overpriced, so I didn't buy them.

items.definition: Not available in a shop at the moment because all of the items have been sold.
examples: I wanted the blue jacket, but it was out of stock in my size.
The website says the laptop will be back in stock next week.

items.definition: Already owned and used by someone else before you buy it.
examples: Most of our furniture is second-hand, and it's in good condition.
She buys second-hand clothes to save money and reduce waste.

items.definition: A written promise from a company that it will repair or replace a product if something goes wrong in a certain period.
examples: The washing machine comes with a two-year guarantee.
Keep the receipt, because you will need it to claim under the guarantee.

items.definition: The place in a shop, or the final stage on a website, where you pay for what you are buying.
examples: There was a long queue at the checkout, so I used the self-service one.
Delivery costs only appear at the checkout, which is annoying.

items.definition: To compare prices and quality in several shops before deciding what to buy.
examples: It's worth shopping around before you buy a new phone.
We shopped around for months before we chose a sofa.

items.definition: To buy a large quantity of something so that you will not run out of it.
examples: We stocked up on tinned food before the storm.
I always stock up on coffee when it's on offer.

items.definition: To spend a lot of money on something enjoyable that you do not really need.
examples: For our anniversary, we splashed out on dinner at a top restaurant.
I don't usually spend much, but I splashed out on a leather jacket.

items.definition: Something that costs far too much money, so that you feel you have been cheated.
examples: Twelve pounds for a sandwich is a complete rip-off.
The tourist menu was a rip-off, so we ate somewhere else.

items.definition: Cloth that is used for making clothes, curtains and other things.
examples: I like this dress because the fabric is soft and doesn't crease.
The shop sells fabric by the metre.

trap.en: A place where goods are made is a factory, not a fabric. Fabric is the cloth that clothes are made from.
trap.es: Una fábrica es a factory. Fabric es la tela de la que está hecha la ropa.

items.definition: Spending or costing much more money than is sensible or necessary.
examples: Buying a new car every year seems extravagant to me.
He's generous but extravagant, and he is always short of money by the end of the month.

trap.en: Extravagant is about spending too much money, not about being strange. A strange or eccentric person is eccentric or unusual.
trap.es: Extravagant se refiere a gastar demasiado dinero, no a ser raro. Para «extravagante» en el sentido de excéntrico se usa eccentric u odd.
